question: In 1835, who developed the process of applying a thin layer of metallic silver to one side of a clear glass pane and created the first mirror?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Justus von Liebig**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Justus von Liebig (1803-1873) was a **German chemist** and is often referred to as the **father of modern organic chemistry**.
 
• In 1835, Justus von Liebig developed a process to coat glass with metallic silver, resulting in the creation of the **first modern mirror.**
 
• Liebig's work in agriculture led to the **development of fertilizers**, which improved crop yields and agricultural practices.
 
• Liebig received various honors for his contributions to science, including being elected as a** member of several prestigious scientific societies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **C.V. Raman:**

 
 
• An Indian physicist known for his discovery of the **Raman Effect** in 1928, which explained the scattering of light and led to advancements in spectroscopy.
 
• He received the **Nobel Prize** in Physics in **1930** for his work.
 
 
 
• **Victor Francis Hess:**
 
 
• An Austrian physicist recognized for discovering **cosmic rays** in **1912**, which contributed significantly to the field of high-energy physics.
 
• He won the **Nobel Prize** in Physics in **1936** for his contributions to the study of cosmic radiation.
 
 
 
• **C.H. Townes:**
 
 
• An American physicist known for co-developing the laser and maser technologies, which have numerous applications in communication and medicine.
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Prize** in Physics in **1964** for his fundamental work in the field of **quantum** **electronics**.
